turnaround_reason: Coty, the beauty/fragrance maker (CoverGirl, Rimmel, plus prestige licenses Kylie, Burberry, Marc Jacobs), traded down to a $1.82 low on soft consumer beauty demand and a heavy debt load. It is recovering near $2.91 as an aggressive deleveraging program and asset monetizations take hold.
bullish_points: Real deleveraging: net debt cut ~$840M YoY to $2.9B (~3.4x), with a stated path toward 2x, funded by the $750M Wella stake sale and $400M Gucci Beauty license sale back to Kering
Prestige cosmetics has momentum — double-digit sell-out growth led by Kylie, Burberry and the Marc Jacobs launch
H1 FY27 free cash flow guided above $300M — real cash to keep paying down debt
Low absolute share price with high operating leverage means modest EBITDA gains flow disproportionately to equity as debt falls
bearish_points: Debt is still the whole story: $3.3B total debt against $176M cash and a 97% D/E; the equity is a leveraged call on execution
Reported operating and net margins are negative and revenue is barely growing (+1.3%)
Management declined to issue full-year FY27 guidance — restructuring is early and uncertain
Shares sold off after Q4 despite a revenue beat, signaling the market wants proof, not promises
catalyst: Continued net-debt reduction toward the ~2x target and sustained prestige-cosmetics growth shown in FY27 quarterly prints
catalyst_timing: FY27 quarterly results starting Q1 FY27 (calendar late 2026)
suggested_trade: Small speculative spot under $3 as a deleveraging call; size for the balance-sheet risk. Spot only.
key_risk: Beauty demand softens and deleveraging stalls, leaving a still-levered balance sheet exposed
would_skip_if: You avoid highly levered equities or want positive margins before buying
